title: Nhà ở xã hội và hòa nhập · Agree / Disagree
prompt: Some people believe that requiring new housing developments to include affordable homes should be a priority. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

grammar.name: Động từ khuyết thiếu và mức độ khẳng định
grammar.example: Affordable homes within new developments can open access to good locations, although excessive obligations or segregated facilities can undermine both construction and social inclusion.
grammar.why: Trong câu “Affordable homes within new developments can open access to good locations, although excessive obligations or segregated facilities can undermine both construction and social inclusion.”, can điều chỉnh mức độ khẳng định hoặc nghĩa vụ, không tạo một bảo đảm tuyệt đối. Nhà giá phải chăng tại khu có trường và giao thông tốt mở tiếp cận việc làm, không chỉ tạo số căn hộ. Nhân viên y tế ở gần bệnh viện nối vị trí nhà với thời gian và khả năng làm việc.

grammar.name: Đối lập hai mệnh đề
grammar.example: Affordable homes within new developments can open access to good locations, although excessive obligations or segregated facilities can undermine both construction and social inclusion.
grammar.why: Trong câu mở, although nối lợi ích dự kiến với giới hạn thực hiện cụ thể. Đưa rõ hai kiểu thất bại khác nhau: dự án không xây và dự án xây nhưng vẫn phân tầng; nhờ đó phản biện không bị thu hẹp thành một vấn đề chi phí chung.

paragraphs: Affordable homes within new developments can open access to good locations, although excessive obligations or segregated facilities can undermine both construction and social inclusion. I support affordable-home requirements when obligations remain viable and lower-income residents receive comparable access to entrances, facilities and neighbourhood opportunities.

Mixed-income development can reduce spatial exclusion. Access to the same neighbourhood connects lower-income households with transport, schools and employment. A key worker could live near the hospital where that person works. Living near employment can also reduce the time and money spent travelling, making the location of an affordable home part of its practical value. An affordable flat improves inclusion only if its occupants can use the neighbourhood's services and shared facilities on comparable terms with other residents.

Poorly designed requirements can make some developments financially unviable or produce segregated entrances. If obligations are set without regard to project costs, developers may postpone construction, reducing total supply. Alternatively, a scheme may meet its numerical target while giving lower-income residents inferior entrances or facilities, preserving exclusion within an apparently mixed neighbourhood. Viability checks should be transparent, while comparable access to entrances and facilities prevents a nominally mixed development from institutionalising a lower status for poorer residents. Published viability assessments should establish obligations before construction, and access rules should apply to shared entrances and facilities so that poorer residents receive more than a nominal address. Planning rules should assess the number of viable homes delivered and residents' effective access, rather than celebrate nominally mixed development that preserves segregation.
Inclusion requires homes that are actually built and residents who can share local opportunities; a quota achieves little if it stops construction or creates second-class access.
